title: "R API"

## Installation

<!-- docs-check: skip -->
```r
# From a source package (needs Rust 1.85 or later):
install.packages("gridwell_0.1.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

The source package carries the Rust crates it needs, so it builds offline. In a
checkout of the repository, make it with `cargo xtask r-source` and then
`R CMD build target/r-source/gridwell`.

## Parsing

```r
library(gridwell)

json <- paste(readLines("table.json", warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
tbl <- gw_parse_ir(json)
```

`gw_parse_ir()` gives a `gw_table`. Every function takes a `gw_table`, a gt table
(converted on the way in) or IR as a JSON string; `as_gw_table()` turns any of them
into a `gw_table`, and anything else is an error. A `gw_table` can be saved with
`saveRDS()` and read back, and knitr's cache keeps it too.

## Showing a Table

For the [getting-started](../guide/getting-started.qmd#first-table) table:

```r
tbl
#> <gw_table: 2 columns, 2 rows>
#>
#> ┌────────────┬────────────┐
#> │ Name       │      Score │
#> ├────────────┼────────────┤
#> │ Alice      │         95 │
#> │ Bob        │         87 │
#> └────────────┴────────────┘
format(tbl, width = 60)   # the same as lines, the drawing at most 60 wide
```

A table prints as a description (its size, row groups, summary rows and title) and
the table drawn as text, as `gw_render_ansi()` draws it, fitted to the console. The
console gets colors unless it can't show them or `NO_COLOR` is set;
`options(gridwell.color = TRUE)` or `FALSE` decides. An invalid table prints its
validation errors.

In R Markdown and Quarto, a table a chunk returns is shown in the document's format:

| Output | Shown as |
|---|---|
| HTML | HTML, with an id of its own so its styles apply to it alone, marked so Quarto doesn't add Bootstrap's table styling |
| PDF (LaTeX, Beamer) | LaTeX, adding the packages it uses (booktabs, multirow, longtable, tabularx, xcolor, ulem) to the document, with rmarkdown installed |
| Typst | Typst |
| Word, PowerPoint, RTF, others | the table drawn as text; `gw_save()` writes a real one |

`.Rnw` and `.Rhtml` files get LaTeX and HTML, unfenced.

## Validation

```r
errors <- gw_validate(tbl)
if (length(errors) > 0) {
  message("Errors: ", paste(errors, collapse = "; "))
}
```

A valid table can still use a feature a format can't express. `gw_warnings(tbl, format)`
lists those [warnings](../schema/validation.qmd#warnings) for one format, or every
format with `format = NULL` (the default); invalid IR and an unknown format are errors.
A table of a newer minor IR version is warned for first, and `gw_parse_ir()` gives a
`warning()` for one too.

```r
warnings <- gw_warnings(tbl, "latex")
```

## Text Rendering

```r
html   <- gw_render_html(tbl)
latex  <- gw_render_latex(tbl)
typst  <- gw_render_typst(tbl)
rtf    <- gw_render_rtf(tbl)
svg    <- gw_render_svg(tbl)
ansi   <- gw_render_ansi(tbl)
pandoc <- gw_render_pandoc(tbl)
quarto <- gw_render_quarto(tbl)

# Generic by name
html <- gw_render(tbl, "html")

# Writer options: a named list, a JSON string, or named arguments
html <- gw_render(tbl, "html", list(inline_styles = TRUE))
html <- gw_render(tbl, "html", '{"inline_styles": true}')
html <- gw_render_html(tbl, inline_styles = TRUE)

# Every format, with its options and defaults (a data frame)
gw_formats()
```

Passing options as a list needs the jsonlite package. See
[Writer Options](../guide/writer-options.qmd) for each format's options.

## Binary Rendering

```r
docx_raw <- gw_render_docx(tbl)    # raw vector
xlsx_raw <- gw_render_xlsx(tbl)
pptx_raw <- gw_render_pptx(tbl)

# Generic by name
docx_raw <- gw_render_binary(tbl, "docx")
```

## Saving to a File

`gw_save()` renders and writes in one call, for every format: the format comes from
the file extension and the bytes are written unchanged (UTF-8 text, no re-encoding,
no added newline), so there is no `writeLines()` versus `writeBin()` to choose. It
takes any table the other functions take, and returns `path` invisibly.

```r
gt::gt(gt::exibble) |> gw_save("table.rtf")

gw_save(tbl, "output.docx")
gw_save(tbl, "table.tex", booktabs = FALSE)              # writer options as arguments
gw_save(tbl, "table.json", format = "quarto")            # .json is pandoc or quarto
gw_save(tbl, "table.txt")                                # plain text, no ANSI escapes
gw_save(tbl, "table.txt", color = TRUE)                  # keep the escapes
gw_save(tbl, "table.html", standalone = TRUE)            # a full document, not a fragment

# Many tables at once
purrr::walk2(tables, paths, gw_save)
```

| Extension | Format |
|---|---|
| `.html` | html |
| `.tex` | latex |
| `.typ` | typst |
| `.rtf` | rtf |
| `.svg` | svg |
| `.txt` | ansi (plain text unless `color = TRUE`) |
| `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx` | docx, xlsx, pptx |
| `.json` | pandoc or quarto: pass `format` |

Extensions are case-insensitive, and `format` overrides the extension. A missing,
unknown or ambiguous extension is an error, and nothing is written if the table,
format or options are invalid.

## Serialization

```r
json_out <- gw_to_json(tbl)
```

## gt Integration

```r
library(gt)
library(gridwell)

gt_tbl <- gt(exibble, rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group")
html <- gw_render_html(gt_tbl)
tbl <- as_gw_table(gt_tbl)

ir_json <- gt_to_ir(gt_tbl)  # the IR itself
```

`gt_to_ir()` and `gt_to_ir_list()` use gt's own converter, `gt::as_ir()`, once the
installed gt has one, and gridwell's copy until then; pass `emitter = "upstream"` or
`emitter = "gridwell"` to choose. See [gt Integration](../guide/integration-gt.qmd).

## Conformance

`gw_conformance_check()` checks a table's IR against an expected table, for an
emitter's tests. Tables are compared as normalized grids, so style ids, key order
and how styles are written don't matter; the check goes by tiers (L0 valid, L1
structure, L2 content, L3 styling), each including the ones before. The expected
grids for the conformance cases are in the repository's `conformance/` directory
(see its README).

```r
gt_tbl <- gt(exibble)                                   # the exibble_basic case
grid <- gw_conformance_normalize(gt_tbl, tier = "L1")  # a table's grid, as JSON
report <- gw_conformance_check(gt_tbl, grid)           # or the path of a grid file
report$passed       # TRUE
report$tiers        # c(L0 = "pass", L1 = "pass", L2 = "not checked", L3 = "not checked")
report$differences  # a data frame: tier, path, expected, actual
report

testthat::expect_true(
    gw_conformance_check(gt_tbl, "conformance/expected/gt/exibble_basic.json")$passed
)
```

IR that doesn't parse or validate fails L0. In `differences`, `expected` and
`actual` are JSON, and `NA` where that grid has nothing at all.

## Error Handling

Every `gw_render*()` function validates the table first and signals an R error
listing the validation errors if the IR is invalid. Use `gw_validate()` to get them
as a character vector instead. Unknown format names, a binary format passed to
`gw_render()` (or a text one to `gw_render_binary()`), and invalid options are errors
too. `gw_save()` adds errors for an extension it can't infer a format from and for a
file it can't write (naming the path).

```r
tryCatch(
  gw_parse_ir("invalid json"),
  error = function(e) message("Parse error: ", conditionMessage(e))
)
```
